memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But God was very angry when he went, and the angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him. When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand, it turned off the road into a field. Balaam beat it to get it back on the road. - Num 22:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam sets off on his journey, but he is not travelling alone as he thinks. The angel of the Lord stands in the road with a drawn sword, blocking his way. Balaam cannot see it, but his donkey can. The animal turns aside into a field to avoid the danger, and Balaam, blind to the true obstacle, beats it back onto the road.

There is deep irony here. The prophet who claimed to see and hear from God is spiritually blind, while the humble donkey perceives what he cannot. Balaam's stubborn determination to go his own way had dulled his sight. He was pressing forward against an obstacle God had placed there for his good.

Sometimes God puts obstacles in our path out of love. What feels like frustration, a closed door, a delay, an unexpected difficulty, may be God's mercy standing in the way to protect us from harm we cannot see. We often beat against these obstacles in frustration, missing the hand of God behind them.

When your path is blocked, pause before you push through in anger. Ask whether the Lord may be lovingly opposing a road that leads to danger. In Christ, even our hindrances can be gifts, for the Father disciplines those He loves (Heb 12:6). Trust that His obstacles are never without purpose.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Could a frustrating obstacle in your life be God's loving protection?
2. Do you push against closed doors without asking what God is doing?
3. How might delays or hindrances be mercies in disguise?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when my path is blocked, help me to pause and seek Your purpose rather than pushing ahead in frustration. Teach me to trust that even Your obstacles are love. Amen.
